tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: The Company is subject to U.S. federal, state and local income taxes with respect to its allocable share of any taxable income or loss of Magnolia LLC. The amount of income taxes recorded by the Company requires interpretations of complex rules related to the Company’s partnership structure and regulations of various tax jurisdictions throughout the United States. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized based on the tax effects of temporary differences between the carrying amounts on the consolidated financial statements and the tax basis of assets and liabilities, as measured using currently enacted tax rates. These differences will result in taxable income or deductions in future years when the reported amounts of the assets or liabilities are recovered or settled, respectively. Considerable judgment is required in predicting when these events may occur and whether recovery of an asset is more likely than not. Magnolia records deferred tax assets and associated valuation allowances, when appropriate, to reflect amounts more likely than not to be realized based upon Company analysis. Additionally, federal and state income tax returns are generally not filed before the consolidated financial statements are prepared.

lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: For the year ended December 31, 2025, two customers, including their subsidiaries, accounted for 41% and 20% of the Company’s combined oil, natural gas, and NGL revenue.
For the year ended December 31, 2024, three customers, including their subsidiaries, accounted for 31%, 24%, and 12% of the Company’s combined oil, natural gas, and NGL revenue.
For the year ended December 31, 2023, three customers, including their subsidiaries, accounted for 25%, 22%, and 11% of the Company’s combined oil, natural gas, and NGL revenue.
In 2025, there were two purchasers who accounted for an aggregate 61% of the total revenue attributable to Magnolia’s assets.
The prices Magnolia receives for its production and the levels of Magnolia’s production depend on numerous factors beyond Magnolia’s control, which include, without limitation, the following:
Magnolia depends upon a small number of significant purchasers for the sale of most of its oil, natural gas, and NGL production.
Magnolia expects to depend upon these or other significant purchasers for the sale of most of its oil and natural gas production.
Magnolia depends on the services of its senior management and technical personnel.

AI-enabled applications and services may rely on large volumes of data, third-party models, and cloud-based infrastructure, which could increase exposure to data privacy, security, and intellectual property risks.

More broadly, the enactment of climate change-related policies and initiatives across the market at the corporate level and/or investor community level may in the future result in increases in the Company’s compliance costs and other operating costs and have other adverse effects (e.g., greater potential for governmental investigations or litigation, driving down demand for the Company’s products, or stimulating demand for alternative forms of energy that do not rely on combustion of fossil fuels).

Magnolia’s ability to make scheduled payments on or to refinance its indebtedness obligations depends on Magnolia’s financial condition and operating performance, which are subject to financial, business, and other factors, many of which are beyond Magnolia’s control.

If Magnolia is unable to fund its debt service obligations, Magnolia may be forced to reduce or delay investments and capital expenditures, sell assets, seek additional capital, or restructure or refinance existing indebtedness, all of which will depend on the condition of the capital markets and Magnolia’s financial condition at such time.

Magnolia’s ability to meet its expenses and debt obligations and comply with the covenants and restrictions contained therein will depend on its future performance, which will be affected by financial, business, economic, industry, regulatory, and other factors, many of which are beyond Magnolia’s control.

The board of directors’ determination with respect to any such dividends, including the record date, the payment date, and the actual amount of the dividend, will depend upon the Company’s profitability and financial condition, contractual restrictions, restrictions imposed by applicable law, and other factors that the board of directors deems relevant at the time of such determination.
Magnolia’s primary source of liquidity and capital has been its cash flows from operations.

Magnolia’s ability to complete future offerings of equity and debt securities and the timing of these offerings will depend upon various factors, including prevailing market conditions and the Company’s financial condition.
Operating cash flows are the Company’s primary source of liquidity and are impacted, in the short term and long term, by oil and natural gas prices.

The amount and frequency of future dividends is subject to the discretion of the Company’s board of directors and primarily depends on earnings, capital expenditures, debt covenants, and various other factors.
The prices the Company receives for production depend on factors outside of its control, including physical markets, supply and demand, financial markets, and national and international policies.
